recent_articles.title: Mizoram Chief Minister Rings Alarm Bell Over Growing Myanmar Refugee Burden
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma** expressed concern over the increasing number of Myanmar refugees entering the state, citing strain on resources and services. Over 40,000 individuals have sought refuge in Mizoram due to ongoing violence in Myanmar, prompting the state government to initiate biometric registration for displaced persons. The influx has led to significant demographic changes in border villages like Zokhawthar, which is now hosting thousands of refugees. **The Central Government** is also undertaking border fencing projects along the India-Myanmar frontier to address security concerns.

recent_articles.title: Meghalaya and Nagaland CMs call for release of 20 hostages - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Meghalaya** and **Nagaland** Chief Ministers have called for the early release of 20 civilians, including 14 Kukis and six Nagas, allegedly held hostage by armed groups in Manipur. **Conrad K. Sangma**, Meghalaya's Chief Minister, expressed concern over the continued captivity of the villagers and urged all parties to pursue dialogue instead of violence. **Neiphiu Rio**, Nagaland's Chief Minister, also contacted **Amit Shah**, Union Home Minister, expressing his concern over the abduction of six Liangmai Nagas.  **Mr. Shah** assured him that necessary measures would be taken to secure their release and bring the perpetrators to justice.

recent_articles.title: Delhi crime rate against women highest in 2024, Jaipur tops cities - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Delhi** recorded the highest crime rate against women in India in 2024, with a rate of 130.7 cases per lakh women, according to the **National Crime Records Bureau**.  The city was followed by Telangana, Odisha, Haryana, and Rajasthan.  While some states saw declines in crime rates against women between 2020 and 2024, including Assam, Telangana experienced a significant increase. **Jaipur** reported the highest crime rate among surveyed cities at 199.6 cases per lakh women, while **Chennai** had one of the lowest rates.  Major crimes against women declined in 2024, with decreases seen in cruelty by husbands or relatives, kidnapping and abduction, assaults on women, and dowry-related crimes.

recent_articles.title: Ladakh: Towards People’s Rule
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Centre** and representatives of the **Apex Body of Ladakh (ABL)** and **Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA)** have reached an "in-principle" agreement on restoring democracy in Ladakh, providing constitutional safeguards under provisions similar to Article 371 A, F, and G.  These provisions are applicable in states like Nagaland, Sikkim, and Mizoram. The agreement includes granting legislative, executive, and financial powers to elected representatives through a UT-level Assembly, with the elected head having direct administrative control over the entire UT bureaucracy.  The agreement also safeguards land, environment, culture, and jobs under Article 371.  While both parties expressed optimism about this step forward, they emphasized that further discussions are needed before finalizing the proposal.

Min Aung Hlaing** is in India for a five-day visit, which includes talks with **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**. The Myanmarese leader's trip comes less than two months after he assumed office following Myanmar's parliamentary elections.

recent_articles.title: Monsoon keeps India waiting, but brutal rain and hail to crash the party Monday - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** southwest monsoon is experiencing a slight delay in its official onset, but active weather systems are causing heavy rain, thundersqualls, and hailstorms across multiple states. The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** predicts widespread atmospheric activity for Monday, June 1st, with downpours targeting the south peninsular region, while isolated heavy rainfall is expected for Kerala, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, and South Interior Karnataka.  The northeastern states of Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura are also on alert for isolated heavy showers.

recent_articles.title: Transporters pause operations in Manipur in protest against trucker’s killing - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Transporters** in Manipur suspended operations on Saturday, May 30, 2026, protesting the killing of a trucker from West Bengal's Hooghly. The attack on a convoy of food trucks and oil tankers by **Kuki militants** on National Highway 202 disrupted essential supplies to Imphal and beyond.  The drivers demanded increased security measures and action against the attackers, while **Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh** assured the families of the slain driver that their safety is a priority.

recent_articles.title: Nagaland intensifies ASF containment measures; pork sale banned in several districts - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nagaland**'s government has intensified surveillance and containment measures following the outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF).  Several districts have imposed bans and restrictions on pig imports, transportation, and sales to prevent further spread. The **Directorate of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services** is actively engaged in surveillance, containment, awareness campaigns, sample collection, and bio-security measures.  The ASF outbreak has led to the temporary closure of pork shops in several parts of the state and a significant impact on local consumption patterns and livelihoods for pig farmers and traders.

recent_articles.title: SC asks Centre to consider States’ pleas for funds for CCTVs in police stations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** urged the **Union government** to fully implement the Assistance to States and Union Territories for Modernisation of Police (ASUMP) scheme, which provides funds for installing CCTV cameras in police stations and a centralized monitoring dashboard. The court expressed concerns over non-functional CCTV cameras in Udaipur police stations and directed the Centre to consider requests from states for funding.  The ASUMP scheme has been extended until September 30, 2026, with most states initiating steps towards compliance. However, Jharkhand was criticized for not installing any CCTV cameras, despite receiving funds under the scheme. The court also cautioned against releasing funds without due diligence to prevent misappropriation.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Bottom 50% of Nagaland households receive only 18% of total income, says report - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Secretary Sentiyanger Imchen** released a report on income disparity in Nagaland, revealing that the top 5% of households earn nearly 21% of the state's gross income, while the bottom 50% receive only 18%. The report, based on a field survey conducted by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation** (MoSPI) and the University of Hyderabad, found a Gini coefficient of 0.46 for Nagaland, indicating high income inequality.  The study also highlighted that rural areas had a higher income disparity than urban areas.

recent_articles.title: PM Modi on West Bengal election result: ‘Lotus’ is blooming from Gangotri to Gangasagar - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026 results: Counting of votes begins across five States - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Counting of votes for the Assembly elections in five states, including Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and West Bengal, is underway.  **Election Commission of India (ECI)** officials are overseeing the process at designated counting centers across the country. Early trends suggest a tight race in several constituencies with the **DMK** seeking to retain power in Tamil Nadu, while the **AIADMK** and independent candidates like Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam are vying for victory. In Kerala, the ruling Left Democratic Front faces competition from the Opposition United Democratic Front (UDF) and Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA).  Security arrangements have been tightened across all states to ensure a smooth and peaceful counting process.

recent_articles.title: Earth Day 2026: How Nature walks, parks, and trails are sparking a new conservation movement - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rohit Girotra**, co-founder of the Bangalore Butterfly Club (BBC), has seen a surge in interest in butterflies and butterfly-focused activities. The BBC, which began in 2012, now boasts nearly 600 members and offers guided walks at Doresanipalya Forest Research Station.  **Ashok Sengupta**, another BBC co-founder, believes that butterfly watching is an easy portal into the natural world for children. **Isaac Kehimkar**, a naturalist and photographer, has documented over 40 Facebook groups dedicated to butterflies worldwide. These groups have helped raise awareness of these insects through social media and mobile cameras. Butterfly parks and trails are also becoming increasingly popular across India, with locations like Sammilan Shetty's Butterfly Park in Karnataka offering educational programs on butterfly conservation.

recent_articles.title: Constitution Amendment Bill proposes possible change in size of State Assemblies - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Constitution** (One Hundred and Thirty-First Amendment) Bill, 2026, proposes significant changes to State Legislative Assemblies by restarting the delimitation process and removing a long-standing constitutional freeze on seat readjustments. The bill aims to update constituency boundaries based on population changes and will be introduced in a Special Session of Parliament beginning April 16th.  The Delimitation Commission, chaired by a former or sitting Supreme Court judge, will determine the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to each state and redraw parliamentary and Assembly constituencies. Public consultation on draft proposals will precede finalization before the new boundaries take effect for elections after the Commission's final orders are published in the Gazette of India.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by **West Bengal**, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

The byelection, necessitated by the death of sitting BJP MLA Imkong L. Imchen in November 2025, will continue until 4 p.m. today with counting scheduled for May 4th.

recent_articles.title: Logic may not be the right tool to examine faith and belief systems, says SC - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** ruled that courts cannot interfere with religious beliefs and practices, emphasizing that logic is not a suitable tool for examining faith.  **Solicitor General Tushar Mehta**, representing the Union government, argued that reform should originate within religions and that courts cannot judge religious practices as "superstition." He cited the 1972 Seshammal versus State of Tamil Nadu case to emphasize that the state cannot abolish a religion's core beliefs.  The court also discussed the concept of "constitutional morality" and its limitations in determining religious practice, emphasizing the importance of understanding public morality from the perspective of followers within each faith.

recent_articles.title: On Assam campaign trail, Meghalaya CM stresses ‘One Northeast’ mission - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Census 2027 kicks off: How to do self-enumeration: step-by-step guide - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner will conduct the 2027 census, a massive administrative and statistical exercise that collects demographic data on the entire country. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their household information online before enumerators visit, offering flexibility in filling out the census schedule.  The dates for self-enumeration vary by state and union territory, with most starting in April 2026. Census data is expected to be published within 2027 due to the digital nature of the process.

recent_articles.title: NSCN-K aims at religious conversion, demographic consolidation, Arunachal government tells UAPA tribunal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Arunachal Pradesh** government presented evidence to a UAPA tribunal that the **National Socialist Council of Nagaland-Khaplang (NSCN-K)** seeks to convert locals to Christianity and create a homogenous society for a common cause. The group, active in Tirap, Changlang, and Longding districts, has been involved in violence, drug trafficking, and attacks on security forces.  The **Ministry of Home Affairs** (MHA) requested the tribunal to extend the NSCN-K's ban for another five years, citing its involvement in 29 incidents of violence, including kidnappings and extortion. The group is considered a threat by the governments of Nagaland, Manipur, and Arunachal Pradesh.

recent_articles.title: Press Club of India issues election reporting advisory to media - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Press Council of India (PCI)** has issued guidelines for media outlets covering the upcoming elections in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Puducherry. The council advised against "paid news" and urged adherence to journalistic conduct regarding pre-poll and exit polls.  It also cautioned against reporting that promotes enmity or hatred between groups based on religion, race, caste, etc., and emphasized the prohibition of publishing false statements about candidates' personal character.

recent_articles.title: What did the Supreme Court rule on Scheduled Castes and religion? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that a person cannot be considered a member of the Scheduled Caste (SC) if they profess a religion different from Hinduism, Sikhism, or Buddhism. The Court upheld this decision based on the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, which states that individuals who "profess" a religion other than these faiths are not SCs.  The Court emphasized that conversion to any faith not listed in the order results in immediate loss of SC status and associated benefits. The ruling also addressed the question of reconversion to Hinduism, Sikhism, or Buddhism, stating that claimants must provide strong evidence for "reconversion" including renunciation of their previous religion, complete assimilation into the original caste, and acceptance by the community.  The Court acknowledged the complexities surrounding conversion and its impact on Scheduled Tribe (ST) status, emphasizing that ST status is determined by tribal attributes rather than solely based on religious affiliation.

recent_articles.title: ‘Family first’ in BJP list of bypoll candidates in Nagaland, Tripura - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** has chosen candidates for upcoming by-elections in Nagaland and Tripura, reflecting a dynastic trend.  Daochier Imchen will represent the Koridang seat in Nagaland, following his father's death, while Jahar Chakraborti is the BJP candidate from Dharmanagar, Tripura. recent_articles.title: Unfenced border in focus amid arrest of seven foreigners who crossed to Myanmar via porous border - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** and **Myanmar** share a 1,643 km unfenced border with a unique Free Movement Regime (FMR) that allows for limited movement of people without visas or passports.  **The National Investigation Agency (NIA)** has accused seven foreign nationals, including six Ukrainians and a US citizen, of illegally crossing into Myanmar to train armed ethnic groups in weapons handling and drone operations. The **Indian government** has implemented a fencing project along the border with 43 km completed out of the approved 390.39 km, but progress on road infrastructure is also slow.  The **Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS)** approved the project for ₹31,000 crore in March 2024 to address challenges like illegal migration and insurgent activities.

recent_articles.title: Environment Ministry endorses names of 10-member expert committee set up to define Aravalli hills - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article:
## Supreme Court to Get Expert Panel on Aravalli Hills

The Union Environment Ministry has given its approval for a 10-member high-powered expert committee tasked with defining the Aravalli hills and ranges. The ministry, in an affidavit filed before the Supreme Court, supports the proposed committee's composition, which includes experts from various fields like forestry, geology, and academia.  The ministry believes this group is necessary to thoroughly examine the complex issues surrounding the Aravalli region and ensure a comprehensive approach that considers stakeholder input. This follows the Supreme Court’s previous order in December 2023, where it paused all mining activities within the Aravallis due to concerns about the new definition of the region. The court had also requested suggestions for experts who could help define the boundaries and protect the area's environment.
